ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, the medians $AD$ and $BE$ intersect at point $O$. If the area of $\triangle AOE$ is 4, what is the area of the quadrilateral $OECD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect DE,\\
$\because$ AD, BE are medians on sides BC, AC respectively,\\
$\therefore$ D, E are the midpoints of BC, AC respectively,\\
$\therefore$ DE is the midline of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ DE $=\frac{1}{2}AB$, DE $\parallel$ AB,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABO\sim \triangle DEO$, $\triangle CDE\sim \triangle CBA$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{OE}{OB}=\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{1}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{S_{\triangle ABO}}{S_{\triangle AOE}}=\frac{BO}{EO}=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\triangle ABO}=8$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\triangle ABE}=S_{\triangle ABO}+S_{\triangle AOE}=12$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\triangle ABC}=2S_{\triangle ABE}=24$,\\
$\because$ $\frac{S_{\triangle DEO}}{S_{\triangle ABO}}=\left(\frac{DE}{AB}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\triangle DEO}=2$,\\
$\because$ $\frac{S_{\triangle CDE}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\left(\frac{DE}{AB}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\triangle CDE}=6$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\text{quadrilateral} OECD}=S_{\triangle DEO}+S_{\triangle CDE}=\boxed{8}$,
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, the medians $AD$ and $BE$ intersect at point $O$. If the area of $\triangle AOE$ is 4, what is the area of the quadrilateral $OECD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Connect $DE$. Since $AD$ and $BE$ are medians on sides $BC$ and $AC$ respectively, $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of $BC$ and $AC$ respectively. Therefore, $DE$ is the midline of $\triangle ABC$, so $DE=\frac{1}{2}AB$ and $DE\parallel AB$. Hence $\triangle ABO\sim\triangle DEO$ and $\triangle CDE\sim\triangle CBA$. Therefore, $\frac{OE}{OB}=\frac{DE}{AB}=\frac{1}{2}$, so $\frac{S_{\triangle ABO}}{S_{\triangle AOE}}=\frac{BO}{EO}=2$. Since $S_{\triangle AOE}=4$, we get $S_{\triangle ABO}=8$. Thus $S_{\triangle ABE}=S_{\triangle ABO}+S_{\triangle AOE}=12$, and $S_{\triangle ABC}=2S_{\triangle ABE}=24$. Also, $\frac{S_{\triangle DEO}}{S_{\triangle ABO}}=\left(\frac{DE}{AB}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}$, so $S_{\triangle DEO}=2$. And $\frac{S_{\triangle CDE}}{S_{\triangle ABC}}=\left(\frac{DE}{AB}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4}$, so $S_{\triangle CDE}=6$. Therefore, $S_{\text{quadrilateral }OECD}=S_{\triangle DEO}+S_{\triangle CDE}=\boxed{8}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; point D is on side BC, point E is on side AC; line segments AD and BE are drawn inside the triangle and intersect at point O. The problem states that AD and BE are medians, therefore D is the midpoint of BC, E is the midpoint of AC, and O is the intersection point of the two medians. Reasoning: Because AD and BE are medians of triangle ABC, O is the centroid. On median BE, the centroid divides the median in the ratio BO:OE=2:1. On line segment BE, triangles ABO and AOE share the altitude from A to line BE, therefore their area ratio equals the ratio of bases BO and OE, namely [ABO]:[AOE]=2:1. It is known that [AOE]=4, so [ABO]=8, and thus [ABE]=[ABO]+[AOE]=8+4=12. Because BE is the median to AC, E is the midpoint of AC, so the area of triangle ABE is half the area of triangle ABC, hence [ABC]=2×12=24. Also because AD is the median to BC, D is the midpoint of BC, so [ABD]=12. Region ABD is divided by line segment BO into triangle ABO and triangle BOD, therefore [BOD]=[ABD]-[ABO]=12-8=4. Finally, quadrilateral OECD is the region left after removing triangle ABO, triangle AOE, and triangle BOD from the whole triangle ABC, so [OECD]=24-8-4-4=8.
